### Rithm Property Trust Inc. Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results


October 21, 2026


- [Download (opens in new window)](https://s205.q4cdn.com/591211382/files/content_files/RPT_Q3-26-Earnings-Release_Final.pdf)


NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


Rithm Property Trust Inc. (NYSE: RPT, “Rithm Property Trust” or the “Company”) today announced its financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.


**Financial Highlights:**


- GAAP comprehensive income of $1.3 million, or $0.17 per diluted common share (1)(2)
- Book value per common share of $29.82 (1)
- Common dividend of $2.8 million, or $0.36 per common share
- Earnings available for distribution of $1.8 million, or $0.23 per diluted common share (1)(3)

For a reconciliation of Earnings Available for Distribution to GAAP Comprehensive Income, as well as an explanation of this measure, please refer to the section entitled “Non-GAAP Financial Measures and Reconciliation to GAAP Comprehensive Income.”


**Business Highlights**


- Monetized residential mortgage-backed securities investments through the paydown of three securitizations.


- Received $37.3 million of principal balance repayment, generating $20.7 million of net cash proceeds after repayment of related financing.
- Generated earnings available for distribution of $0.17 per diluted common share.


- Invested in an additional $97.0 million unpaid principal balance (“UPB”) of residential transition loans originated by Genesis Capital LLC, with an unfunded commitment of $29.6 million UPB. The purchase was funded with a combination of borrowings under the Company’s repurchase facility and $24.7 million of cash.


**Additional Information**


Dividend Declaration


On October 20, 2026, the Company’s Board of Directors declared a cash dividend of $0.36 per share of common stock to be paid on November 30, 2026, to stockholders of record as of October 30, 2026, and a cash dividend of $0.6171875 per share of the Company’s 9.875% Series C Fixed-to-Floating Rate Cumulative Redeemable Preferred Stock to be paid on November 16, 2026, to preferred stockholders of record as of November 1, 2026 (with an effective record date of October 30, 2026).


Other Matters


The Company will not hold a conference call to discuss its financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. The investor relations team remains available for questions atir@rithmpropertytrust.com .

**NON-GAAP FINANCIAL MEASURES AND RECONCILIATION TO GAAP COMPREHENSIVE INCOME**


The Company has three primary variables that impact its performance: (i) net interest margin on assets held within the investment portfolio; (ii) realized and unrealized gains or losses on assets held within the investment portfolio, including any impairment or reserve for expected credit losses; and (iii) the Company’s operating expenses and taxes.


“Earnings available for distribution” is a non-GAAP financial measure of the Company’s operating performance, which is used by management to evaluate the Company’s performance excluding:


- Net income and losses attributable to noncontrolling interests;
- Certain realized and unrealized gains and losses (including impairment) on certain assets and liabilities; and
- Other adjustments which primarily consist of amortization expense, non-capitalized transaction-related expenses related to legal, valuation and other professional service fees incurred in connection with certain investment acquisitions and deferred taxes.


In computing earnings available for distribution, the Company excludes the items listed above because management does not consider them representative of the Company's core operating performance or of cash available for distribution to stockholders. These adjustments generally fall into three categories: items that are non-cash in nature; items that, while a part of the Company's recurring operations, are subject to significant variability and are therefore generally limited to a potential indicator of future economic performance; and items that relate to the acquisition of investments rather than to ongoing operations.


Management believes that the adjustments to compute “earnings available for distribution” specified above allow investors and analysts to readily identify and track the operating performance of the assets that form the core of the Company’s activity, assist in comparing the core operating results between periods and enable investors to evaluate the Company’s current core performance using the same financial measure that management uses to operate the business. Management also utilizes earnings available for distribution as a financial measure in its decision-making process relating to improvements to the underlying fundamental operations of the Company’s investments, as well as the allocation of resources between those investments, and management also relies on earnings available for distribution as an indicator of the results of such decisions. As such earnings available for distribution is not intended to reflect all of the Company’s activity and should be considered as only one of the factors used by management in assessing the Company’s performance, along with GAAP comprehensive income which is inclusive of all of the Company’s activities.


The Company views earnings available for distribution as a consistent financial measure of its portfolio’s ability to generate income for distribution to common stockholders. Earnings available for distribution does not represent and should not be considered as a substitute for, or superior to, comprehensive income or as a substitute for, or superior to, cash flows from operating activities, each as determined in accordance with GAAP, and the Company’s calculation of this financial measure may not be comparable to similarly entitled financial measures reported by other companies. Furthermore, to maintain qualification as a REIT, U.S. federal income tax law generally requires that the Company distribute at least 90% of its REIT taxable income annually, determined without regard to the deduction for dividends paid and excluding net capital gains. Because the Company views earnings available for distribution as a consistent financial measure of its ability to generate income for distribution to common stockholders, earnings available for distribution is one metric, but not the exclusive metric, that the Company’s board of directors uses to determine the amount, if any, and the payment date of dividends on common stock. However, earnings available for distribution should not be considered as an indication of the Company’s taxable income, a guaranty of its ability to pay dividends or as a proxy for the amount of dividends it may pay, as earnings available for distribution excludes certain items that impact its cash needs.
